claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
The initiation and progression of phase transformation in the high-temperature BCC phase are governed by chemical short-range order within the BCC matrix.
Chemical short-range order lowers the local free energy.
Chemical short-range order reduces the kinetic barrier for nucleating a secondary phase.
Phase transformation is triggered once a critical short-range-order threshold is reached.
High-temperature annealing stabilizes the BCC phase in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
The proposed high-temperature annealing produces uniform composition and minimal prior ordering.
Cooling into 800–900°C drives progressive formation of local chemical short-range-order clusters in the BCC matrix.
Composition-dependent chemical interactions in the alloy drive short-range-order formation as temperature decreases.
Short-range-order clusters create locally favorable environments for secondary-phase nucleation.
Short-range-order development will produce increased diffuse scattering during in situ XRD.
Short-range-order development will produce weak superlattice reflections.
The onset of measurable short-range order will temporally correlate with secondary-phase nucleation.
Rapid quenching retains the high-temperature BCC state while preventing substantial short-range-order evolution.
Within 800–900°C, diffusion is sufficiently active to develop short-range order while the temperature is not high enough to prevent ordering.
